answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token bond before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that bond when independently verifiable fraud is proven. A plume of fresh accounts does not multiply influence for free: every sybil needs its own capital, which remains unavailable elsewhere, and discovered accounts lose it. The onyx ledger makes deposits and penalties auditable, while a forge can produce identities but cannot forge the locked collateral or erase the cost of replacing slashed agents.
